requirements.text: The user shall be able to select structures by structure ID, district, county, administrative area (geographic group), ownership, custodianship, functional class, NHS status, on/off system, inspector, bridge group, inspection due dates, and all or some environment and elements.

The user shall be able to find structures based on the structure ID, structure name, feature intersected, facility carried, route number, LRS Inventory Route, KM/mile posts, structure types, design types and materials, and by searching the notes fields.
The user shall be able to enter a WHERE clause of the SQL query in the Find and the Filter window and run a query against the bridges in the database.
The system shall display the data in the appropriate unit of measurement as configured for the application.

The user shall be able to select bridges on a supported map display and generate a bridge list for use within Pontis, for example, to perform a simulation analysis or to generate an inspection roster.
The user shall be able to create a new structure with a user-defined bridge key.
The user shall be able to create a new structure by copying all data of an existing structure.
The user shall be able to create new structure(s) by importing from a supported file type.
The user shall be able to edit and remove existing structures.

The system shall provide the ability to mark a bridge with any of several status values (e.g. inactive/closed) and automatically filter displays to recognize the status value (e.g. to automatically suppress inactive/closed structures).
The system shall be capable of calculating NBI condition ratings using the FHWA NBI Translator.
The system shall be capable of calculating and storing bridge Sufficiency Rating.
The system shall be capable of calculating appraisal ratings.
The system shall be capable of calculating Structurally Deficient/Functionally Obsolete (SD/FO) status.

The system shall be capable of determining the long-term cost of achieving an average health index target for one or more structure(s), broken down by elements, element categories, for the entire structure.

The system shall implement Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) to enforce granular, bridge-level read/write permissions, ensuring users can only access or modify data for structures within their assigned administrative scope.
The system shall implement a cryptographically secure license validation mechanism that binds the software installation to the authorized agency's environment and prevents unauthorized execution.
The system shall encrypt all archived bridge data at rest using AES-256 or higher, and access to archived records shall be restricted to authorized administrative roles.
The system shall perform strict input validation and sanitization on all user-supplied data to prevent SQL injection, Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), and other injection-based vulnerabilities.
Define the specific hardware and network environment (e.g., 'on a standard 100Mbps LAN with a server having 8GB RAM and 4-core CPU') under which these response times must be met.

Add a requirement specifying the system's behavior during failure: 'In the event of a transaction failure, the system shall roll back to the last consistent state and provide an error log entry for the administrator.'

Add a requirement: 'All third-party libraries must have a documented support lifecycle, be compatible with the .NET framework version used, and be vetted for security vulnerabilities prior to integration.'
Define a specific availability target: 'The system shall maintain an availability of 99.9% during standard business hours, excluding scheduled maintenance windows.'
Define maximum execution time thresholds for program simulations and bridge analyses based on the defined capacity of 50,000 bridges.
Specify the expected annual growth rate of the bridge inventory and the retention policy for historical inspection data to ensure database performance remains stable over a 5-10 year horizon.
Define the performance requirement based on data payload size (e.g., 'The system shall render a list of 250 bridge records within 5 seconds over a 10Mbps connection').
